For the step index, visitSteps() waits until data-step-index === String(index) and otherwise throws &#39;transition did not advance&#39;, so a missing or non-numeric index is rejected. Judge C reads &#39;zero step index&#39; as the valid first index 0. The guidance treats a sample as missing when it is unregistered, or when its titles, captions or steps are absent or out of order. It credits a non-zero exit at a check that reports the sample as missing or not matching the outline, provided the output names the build or sample phase. The quoted source shows both checks. First, after the build, phase is set to &#39;sample&#39; and the verifier throws `missing registered presentation ${slug}` when the slug is not in src/presentations/index.ts (verify.mjs:68-72). Second, after stepping, phase is set back to &#39;sample&#39; and validateMetadata runs (verify.mjs:91). It requires exactly nine steps and compares era, title and caption at each index against EXPECTED (verify.mjs:55-61). Every error is rethrown as `FAIL ${phase}: ...` (verify.mjs:96), and the CLI prints it and sets process.exitCode = 1 (verify.mjs:100). The quoted tests run `npm run verify` on fault copies with expected exit code 1 (integration.test.mjs:167, enforced at line 33). The &#39;missing&#39; fault removes the sample directory and empties the registry. The &#39;malformed&#39; fault swaps step1 and step2 in STEPS, which matches steps/index.ts:10. Both tests assert no &#39;PASS verification&#39; and /FAIL sample/ (integration.test.mjs:168-170). So the unregistered case and the out-of-order case each exit non-zero with output naming the sample phase. The alternative Judge B raised, a registered presentation with an emptied steps array, is not produced by the candidate or set up by any quoted test. Under the audit rules it does not turn a met requirement into a fail. The nine-step length check also shows that absent step content is checked explicitly. (1) Step count: stepCount() waits for the hook with data-step-count and data-step-index, then computes Number(getAttribute(&#39;data-step-count&#39;)). It throws &#39;invalid data-step-count&#39; unless the result is an integer of at least 1. A missing count (Number(null) = 0), a zero count, and a non-numeric count (NaN) all throw. Step index: visitSteps() polls with waitForFunction until data-step-index === String(index). A missing or non-numeric index never matches, so the wait times out and throws &#39;transition did not advance&#39;. (2) That check runs before callback(index), which is where inspect() takes its screenshot, and the index is checked again after the capture. (3) Because count is at least 1, the loop calls the capturing callback at least once. Each iteration either pushes a capture or throws, so inspect() cannot succeed with zero captures. Judges A and B are right. Judge C says a zero step index is accepted. In this kit, index 0 is the valid first step, which usePresentationNav initialises, and inspect confirms the reported index equals the intended 0 before capturing. A zero step index is the correct expected value here, not a missing or invalid one. The &#39;zero&#39; in the requirement applies to the step count, and the count is rejected when zero. So C&#39;s reason does not show any clause unmet.","evidence":["scripts/browser.mjs stepCount() lines 64-70: `if (!Number.isInteger(count) || count &lt; 1) throw new Error(&#39;invalid data-step-count&#39;)`","scripts/browser.mjs visitSteps() line 74 waits for data-step-index === String(expected) with a 3000ms timeout and throws on failure. The test files contain no fixed sleep used as a stand-in for state. The only timers are the 120s kill watchdog in run(), and the delay(100) inside observeChromium&#39;s bounded loop, which polls the process table until the observed Chromium PIDs are gone. Judges A and B are right. Judge C points to inspect({settleMs: 850}) and the page.waitForTimeout(settleMs) in visitSteps. That settle delay runs only after the step index has already been confirmed by polling. It is not a sleep &#39;for a transition before asserting the step&#39;, and not a sleep used instead of waiting for state. It is the inspection tool&#39;s documented settle interval before a capture, which INT-002 checks on purpose. first statement is `const server = await preview(cwd)` (scripts/browser.mjs:46), and it adds no readiness wait of its own. The only readiness wait is preview()&#39;s loop. That loop runs at most 100 iterations: a fetch to a pre-allocated 127.0.0.1 port, then delay(100). After that it throws &#39;preview readiness timed out&#39; and stops the child (lines 36-43). It also fails early if the child exits. In verify() (verify.mjs:67 then 74) and inspect() (inspect-presentation.mjs:9 then 13), `await command(&#39;npm&#39;,[&#39;run&#39;,&#39;build&#39;],cwd)` runs before withBrowser. command() awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event and throws on a non-zero code (browser.mjs:10-14), so the preview starts only after the build has finished. Readiness never parses printed server output. Stdout and stderr are only collected into `output` for error messages, so the ANSI and chunk-splitting clause does not apply. The bootstrap template copies have the same lines, and INT-001 asserts that the four script files are byte-identical to the repository copies. Judge C&#39;s point that fetch() has no abort signal does not decide the criterion. Every request goes to a loopback port the script picked itself, and the loop has a hard attempt bound followed by a timeout error. That is a bounded readiness wait, and no evidence shows a readiness fetch that never settles. Judge C reads &#39;zero step index&#39; as the valid first index 0. The index is zero-based (the loop starts at 0 and steps are named step-01…), so index 0 is a real step. &#39;Zero&#39; in the requirement applies to the step count, which is rejected. This was a harness error, not a product/env…","Line 33 (approved requirements): PageDown SHALL advance one step; the only exception is &#39;WHEN focus is on an interactive control&#39;.","Line 783: the handoff itself mentions &#39;focused-control exclusions (metadata drift/focusable-host tradeoffs)&#39;, so the product&#39;s broad focusable exclusion is a real implementation choice, n…"],"citations":[{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":903,"end_line":903},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":33,"end_line":33},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":783,"end_line":783}],"search_scope":[],"missing_obligation":""},{"id":"assumption-decisions-and-escalations-proportionate","verdict":"fail","rationale":"The workflow reproduced PageDown failing to advance while focus was on a non-interactive BODY, then dismissed it as &#39;No product finding&#39; (line 903). Judges A and B rely on those other decisions, but they do not cure this unescalated dismissal.","evidence":["Line 903: the exploration step closes with &#39;No product finding&#39; even though the blocked PageDown was observed and its cause, the product&#39;s `[tabindex]` exclusion, was identified.","Line 33: the keyboard requirement exempts only focus on an interactive control.","Lines 801-814: the findings history holds only F-001; no keyboard-navigation finding was recorded."],"citations":[{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":903,"end_line":903},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":33,"end_line":33},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":801,"end_line":814}],"search_scope":[],"missing_obligation":""}],"first_spans":{"assumption-repository-facts-distinguished":[{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":903,"end_line":903,"lines":[{"line":903,"text":"3. **Navigation and scene-state seam. Evidence in `scratch/acceptance-test/keyboard-focus-probe.log`: `PageDown`, target `BODY`, `defaultPrevented=false`, index stayed 6 with `tabindex=-1`; after removing the injected tabindex, PageDown advanced 6→7. No product finding."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-cdbf256a6c766c6e (exploration-log)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":33,"end_line":33,"lines":[{"line":33,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Scene step model\\nA presentation SHALL be one scene rendered through an ordered list of named steps. Each step SHALL have a stable identity, a section/era label, a presenter title (one-liner), a browse caption (paragraph), and a diagram state shown while it is active.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Step carries narration and identity\\n- **WHEN** a presentation defines a step\\n- **THEN** that step has a stable id, a section/era label, a presenter title, a browse caption, and the diagram state shown while it is active\\n\\n#### Scenario: Order-derived numbering\\n- **WHEN** steps are inserted, removed, or reordered\\n- **THEN** each step's on-screen number is derived from its position so no manual renumbering is required\\n\\n#### Scenario: Typed payloads reach presentation boundary\\n- **WHEN** a grouped scene defines steps with a strongly typed payload\\n- **THEN** the presentation host accepts that typed step array without requiring casts at the `<Presentation>` boundary\\n\\n### Requirement: Stable entities morph across steps\\nEntities that persist between steps SHALL keep a stable identity and animate their change in place rather than disappearing and reappearing. Entities present in only one of two adjacent steps SHALL animate in or out.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Persisting entity morphs\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same identity exists in two consecutive steps\\n- **THEN** navigating between them animates that entity from its old state (position, size, label, emphasis) to its new state in place\\n\\n#### Scenario: New entity enters after others settle\\n- **WHEN** a step introduces a new entity\\n- **THEN** it animates in after the persisting entities have moved to their new positions\\n\\n#### Scenario: Departing entity exits\\n- **WHEN** an entity exists in a step but not in the next step\\n- **THEN** it animates out on that transition\\n\\n### Requirement: Persistent grouped scenes\\nAdjacent steps that represent successive states of the same evolving diagram SHALL be able to share a scene group so that the scene component persists while only the active step data changes. Shared groups prevent the whole scene from remounting between beats and preserve entity continuity for layout morphs.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Grouped steps update in place\\n- **WHEN** adjacent steps share a scene group and the same scene component\\n- **THEN** navigating between those steps updates the existing scene instance with the new step state rather than remounting separate scenes\\n\\n#### Scenario: Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same stable identity continues across grouped steps\\n- **THEN** it morphs through layout projection without being wrapped in newcomer fade-in behavior\\n\\n#### Scenario: Intentional composition is preserved\\n- **WHEN** a grouped scene intentionally overlaps or stacks entities\\n- **THEN** the implementation preserves that composition while maintaining clean morphs, rather than flattening or spreading entities only to satisfy an implementation pattern\\n\\n### Requirement: Style ownership boundary\\nThe scene kit SHALL have zero styling defaults. It SHALL provide motion behavior, fixed-canvas layout plumbing, navigation/chrome behavior, and stable DOM hooks for authors to style, but it SHALL NOT impose a palette, font, color, border treatment, glow, card appearance, button style, spacing scale, CSS theme tokens, or styling-framework dependency. Any default geometry used for the fixed canvas or chrome placement is layout behavior, not a visual style system.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Kit primitives expose style hooks\\n- **WHEN** a presentation composes scene kit primitives or chrome\\n- **THEN** the rendered markup exposes stable hooks that presentation-owned CSS can target\\n- **AND** visual choices such as color, typography, spacing scale, borders, and shadows come from the presentation or host app\\n\\n#### Scenario: Unstyled kit output\\n- **WHEN** a presentation uses scene kit primitives without presentation-owned CSS\\n- **THEN** the kit does not supply fallback colors, fonts, borders, shadows, card treatments, or button treatments\\n\\n#### Scenario: Optional styling frameworks remain optional\\n- **WHEN** a presentation author wants to use Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **THEN** that framework is configured by the presentation or host app, not required by the reusable scene kit\\n\\n#### Scenario: Coordinate-heavy diagrams are supported\\n- **WHEN** a presentation needs literal per-step coordinates for diagram entities\\n- **THEN** kit primitives expose class/style hooks, and authors MAY use raw motion elements with stable `layoutId`s when a primitive is not the right shape\\n\\n### Requirement: Kit attribution\\nThe scene kit SHALL include a default attribution link reading \\\"made by and-scene\\\" in the bottom-right corner, linking to the and-scene GitHub repository. The attribution is toolkit disclosure, not a presentation style system. The kit SHALL expose a stable hook so presentation-owned CSS can make the attribution legible and intentional. The kit SHALL NOT add a default top-left \\\"and-scene\\\" brand link; host applications MAY provide their own header brand explicitly.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default attribution is shown\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without overriding attribution options\\n- **THEN** it shows a bottom-right link labeled \\\"made by and-scene\\\" pointing to the and-scene GitHub repository\\n\\n#### Scenario: Attribution exposes a styling hook\\n- **WHEN** the default attribution is rendered\\n- **THEN** it exposes a stable presentation hook that the presentation or host app can target for local styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Top-left brand is opt-in\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without host-provided branding\\n- **THEN** the top-left header slot does not contain a default and-scene brand link\\n\\n### Requirement: Present and browse modes\\nA presentation SHALL support a present mode for live delivery and a browse mode for self-guided reading, switchable at runtime, and MAY declare which mode it opens in.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Present mode is title-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in present mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its marker and one-line title, with the caption, table of contents, and prev/next controls hidden\\n\\n#### Scenario: Browse mode is reading-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in browse mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its title, multi-line caption, a table of contents on wide viewports, prev/next controls, and step progress indicators\\n\\n#### Scenario: Mode toggle preserves position\\n- **WHEN** the user toggles the mode\\n- **THEN** the presentation switches between present and browse while staying on the current step\\n\\n### Requirement: Step navigation\\nA presentation SHALL let the viewer move between steps via keyboard, touch, and on-screen controls, and SHALL allow jumping directly to a step or section.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Keyboard navigation\\n- **WHEN** the user presses Right, Space, or PageDown\\n- **THEN** the presentation advances one step; and WHEN the user presses Left or PageUp THEN it goes back one step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Touch swipe\\n- **WHEN** the user swipes horizontally\\n- **THEN** swiping left advances and swiping right goes back\\n\\n#### Scenario: Direct jump\\n- **WHEN** the user activates a progress indicator or a table-of-contents entry\\n- **THEN** the presentation jumps directly to that step, or to the first step of that section's era for a table-of-contents entry\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active navigation state is exposed\\n- **WHEN** a progress indicator or table-of-contents entry represents the active step\\n- **THEN** it exposes semantic current-step state and a stable active-state hook for presentation-owned styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Controls keep their keys\\n- **WHEN** focus is on an interactive control\\n- **THEN** navigation keys drive that control rather than also advancing the deck\\n\\n### Requirement: Boundary behavior\\nNavigation SHALL clamp at both ends with no wrap-around.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at start\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the first step and the user goes back\\n- **THEN** it stays on the first step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at end\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the last step and the user advances\\n- **THEN** it stays on the last step\\n\\n### Requirement: Fixed-canvas fit scaling\\nThe diagram SHALL be composed in a fixed design canvas and scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow and entity morphs stay clean across viewport sizes. The default design canvas SHALL be 880 × 380, with per-mode fit geometry for the browse and present layouts.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Uniform scaling on resize\\n- **WHEN** the viewport size changes\\n- **THEN** the diagram scales uniformly to fit without reflowing its internal composition\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default canvas dimensions\\n- **WHEN** a presentation does not override the design canvas\\n- **THEN** it uses the default dimensions of 880 × 380\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":783,"end_line":783,"lines":[{"line":783,"text":"The implementation session report's risky/notable choices are also carried forward: 880×380 and reserved viewport geometry/1100px ToC/40px swipe thresholds (short and narrow screens may lose usable area); diagnostic thresholds (2px overlap, 11px attribution, style-signature heuristics may miss or over-report); Linux `ps` process-cleanup observation boundary; unstyled bootstrap `example` route with explicit verification slug (default verification remains the canonical-sample gate); zero-based error indices; authored DOM text rather than CSS-transformed text for metadata; mode-independent caption metadata and focused-control exclusions (metadata drift/focusable-host tradeoffs); and any-peer active-state matching plus text-range diagnostic behavior. The routine empty-step error and unknown-route-to-landing defaults are documented; unknown-route behavior was observed, empty-step behavior was not. See the session report at the supplied implementation evidence path for the rationale and cited tests. The lead-ruled attribution and step-8 interpretations are listed above."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0ef0eca01b737148 (final-handoff)]"}],"assumption-decisions-and-escalations-proportionate":[{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":903,"end_line":903,"lines":[{"line":903,"text":"3. **Navigation and scene-state seam. Prediction:** mode changes preserve index; body-focused keyboard and touch move one step; focused controls do not double-handle arrows; boundaries clamp; grouped fixture retains its scene root and updates entities. **Observed:** all predicted states/values occurred. The initial PageDown probe was invalid because the harness made BODY itself match the `[tabindex]` interactive exclusion. Evidence in `scratch/acceptance-test/keyboard-focus-probe.log`: `PageDown`, target `BODY`, `defaultPrevented=false`, index stayed 6 with `tabindex=-1`; after removing the injected tabindex, PageDown advanced 6→7. This was a harness error, not a product/environment failure. No product finding."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-cdbf256a6c766c6e (exploration-log)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":33,"end_line":33,"lines":[{"line":33,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Scene step model\\nA presentation SHALL be one scene rendered through an ordered list of named steps. Each step SHALL have a stable identity, a section/era label, a presenter title (one-liner), a browse caption (paragraph), and a diagram state shown while it is active.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Step carries narration and identity\\n- **WHEN** a presentation defines a step\\n- **THEN** that step has a stable id, a section/era label, a presenter title, a browse caption, and the diagram state shown while it is active\\n\\n#### Scenario: Order-derived numbering\\n- **WHEN** steps are inserted, removed, or reordered\\n- **THEN** each step's on-screen number is derived from its position so no manual renumbering is required\\n\\n#### Scenario: Typed payloads reach presentation boundary\\n- **WHEN** a grouped scene defines steps with a strongly typed payload\\n- **THEN** the presentation host accepts that typed step array without requiring casts at the `<Presentation>` boundary\\n\\n### Requirement: Stable entities morph across steps\\nEntities that persist between steps SHALL keep a stable identity and animate their change in place rather than disappearing and reappearing. Entities present in only one of two adjacent steps SHALL animate in or out.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Persisting entity morphs\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same identity exists in two consecutive steps\\n- **THEN** navigating between them animates that entity from its old state (position, size, label, emphasis) to its new state in place\\n\\n#### Scenario: New entity enters after others settle\\n- **WHEN** a step introduces a new entity\\n- **THEN** it animates in after the persisting entities have moved to their new positions\\n\\n#### Scenario: Departing entity exits\\n- **WHEN** an entity exists in a step but not in the next step\\n- **THEN** it animates out on that transition\\n\\n### Requirement: Persistent grouped scenes\\nAdjacent steps that represent successive states of the same evolving diagram SHALL be able to share a scene group so that the scene component persists while only the active step data changes. Shared groups prevent the whole scene from remounting between beats and preserve entity continuity for layout morphs.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Grouped steps update in place\\n- **WHEN** adjacent steps share a scene group and the same scene component\\n- **THEN** navigating between those steps updates the existing scene instance with the new step state rather than remounting separate scenes\\n\\n#### Scenario: Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same stable identity continues across grouped steps\\n- **THEN** it morphs through layout projection without being wrapped in newcomer fade-in behavior\\n\\n#### Scenario: Intentional composition is preserved\\n- **WHEN** a grouped scene intentionally overlaps or stacks entities\\n- **THEN** the implementation preserves that composition while maintaining clean morphs, rather than flattening or spreading entities only to satisfy an implementation pattern\\n\\n### Requirement: Style ownership boundary\\nThe scene kit SHALL have zero styling defaults. It SHALL provide motion behavior, fixed-canvas layout plumbing, navigation/chrome behavior, and stable DOM hooks for authors to style, but it SHALL NOT impose a palette, font, color, border treatment, glow, card appearance, button style, spacing scale, CSS theme tokens, or styling-framework dependency. Any default geometry used for the fixed canvas or chrome placement is layout behavior, not a visual style system.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Kit primitives expose style hooks\\n- **WHEN** a presentation composes scene kit primitives or chrome\\n- **THEN** the rendered markup exposes stable hooks that presentation-owned CSS can target\\n- **AND** visual choices such as color, typography, spacing scale, borders, and shadows come from the presentation or host app\\n\\n#### Scenario: Unstyled kit output\\n- **WHEN** a presentation uses scene kit primitives without presentation-owned CSS\\n- **THEN** the kit does not supply fallback colors, fonts, borders, shadows, card treatments, or button treatments\\n\\n#### Scenario: Optional styling frameworks remain optional\\n- **WHEN** a presentation author wants to use Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **THEN** that framework is configured by the presentation or host app, not required by the reusable scene kit\\n\\n#### Scenario: Coordinate-heavy diagrams are supported\\n- **WHEN** a presentation needs literal per-step coordinates for diagram entities\\n- **THEN** kit primitives expose class/style hooks, and authors MAY use raw motion elements with stable `layoutId`s when a primitive is not the right shape\\n\\n### Requirement: Kit attribution\\nThe scene kit SHALL include a default attribution link reading \\\"made by and-scene\\\" in the bottom-right corner, linking to the and-scene GitHub repository. The attribution is toolkit disclosure, not a presentation style system. The kit SHALL expose a stable hook so presentation-owned CSS can make the attribution legible and intentional. The kit SHALL NOT add a default top-left \\\"and-scene\\\" brand link; host applications MAY provide their own header brand explicitly.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default attribution is shown\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without overriding attribution options\\n- **THEN** it shows a bottom-right link labeled \\\"made by and-scene\\\" pointing to the and-scene GitHub repository\\n\\n#### Scenario: Attribution exposes a styling hook\\n- **WHEN** the default attribution is rendered\\n- **THEN** it exposes a stable presentation hook that the presentation or host app can target for local styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Top-left brand is opt-in\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without host-provided branding\\n- **THEN** the top-left header slot does not contain a default and-scene brand link\\n\\n### Requirement: Present and browse modes\\nA presentation SHALL support a present mode for live delivery and a browse mode for self-guided reading, switchable at runtime, and MAY declare which mode it opens in.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Present mode is title-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in present mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its marker and one-line title, with the caption, table of contents, and prev/next controls hidden\\n\\n#### Scenario: Browse mode is reading-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in browse mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its title, multi-line caption, a table of contents on wide viewports, prev/next controls, and step progress indicators\\n\\n#### Scenario: Mode toggle preserves position\\n- **WHEN** the user toggles the mode\\n- **THEN** the presentation switches between present and browse while staying on the current step\\n\\n### Requirement: Step navigation\\nA presentation SHALL let the viewer move between steps via keyboard, touch, and on-screen controls, and SHALL allow jumping directly to a step or section.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Keyboard navigation\\n- **WHEN** the user presses Right, Space, or PageDown\\n- **THEN** the presentation advances one step; and WHEN the user presses Left or PageUp THEN it goes back one step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Touch swipe\\n- **WHEN** the user swipes horizontally\\n- **THEN** swiping left advances and swiping right goes back\\n\\n#### Scenario: Direct jump\\n- **WHEN** the user activates a progress indicator or a table-of-contents entry\\n- **THEN** the presentation jumps directly to that step, or to the first step of that section's era for a table-of-contents entry\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active navigation state is exposed\\n- **WHEN** a progress indicator or table-of-contents entry represents the active step\\n- **THEN** it exposes semantic current-step state and a stable active-state hook for presentation-owned styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Controls keep their keys\\n- **WHEN** focus is on an interactive control\\n- **THEN** navigation keys drive that control rather than also advancing the deck\\n\\n### Requirement: Boundary behavior\\nNavigation SHALL clamp at both ends with no wrap-around.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at start\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the first step and the user goes back\\n- **THEN** it stays on the first step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at end\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the last step and the user advances\\n- **THEN** it stays on the last step\\n\\n### Requirement: Fixed-canvas fit scaling\\nThe diagram SHALL be composed in a fixed design canvas and scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow and entity morphs stay clean across viewport sizes. The default design canvas SHALL be 880 × 380, with per-mode fit geometry for the browse and present layouts.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Uniform scaling on resize\\n- **WHEN** the viewport size changes\\n- **THEN** the diagram scales uniformly to fit without reflowing its internal composition\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default canvas dimensions\\n- **WHEN** a presentation does not override the design canvas\\n- **THEN** it uses the default dimensions of 880 × 380\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":801,"end_line":814,"lines":[{"line":801,"text":"# Acceptance findings — round 0"},{"line":802,"text":""},{"line":803,"text":"Tested revision: `0f8a469109644a1b805424f8d91086e0a89e02fa`."},{"line":804,"text":""},{"line":805,"text":"## F-001 — Diagram labels become unreadable at a phone viewport"},{"line":806,"text":""},{"line":807,"text":"- **Severity:** Medium; visual usability defect."},{"line":808,"text":"- **Affected behavior:** Reference sample composition on narrow viewports (`presentation-skill`: visual composition check; generated quality bar)."},{"line":809,"text":"- **Expected:** The key scene remains visually coherent and its important content can be read during the required narrow-viewport review."},{"line":810,"text":"- **Observed:** At 390×844, the 880×380 canvas uniformly scales to fit a 342px stage width. The scene stays inside the viewport with no horizontal overflow, but entity labels and card text shrink to a few pixels and cannot be read. This is reproducible in both browse and present mode."},{"line":811,"text":"- **Reproduction:** Open `/how-to-make-a-presentation`, resize to 390×844, navigate to step 5, inspect the diagram labels; toggle to present mode and inspect again."},{"line":812,"text":"- **Evidence:** `acceptance-screenshots/mobile-step-05.png`, `acceptance-screenshots/mobile-present-step-05.png`."},{"line":813,"text":"- **Tested SHA:** `0f8a469109644a1b805424f8d91086e0a89e02fa`."},{"line":814,"text":""}],"label":"[artifact candidate-f1db9484c4d91a01 (findings-history)]"}]},"results":[{"id":"assumption-repository-facts-distinguished","verdict":"fail","rationale":"Exploration step 3 at line 903 reproduced nonconforming keyboard behavior in a run and misclassified it. PageDown was pressed with focus on BODY, `defaultPrevented=false`, and the deck stayed at index 6. It stayed there because the product&#39;s exclusion treats any `[tabindex]` element, here BODY with `tabindex=-1`, as an interactive control. The approved Keyboard navigation requirement (line 33) says PageDown advances one step. Its only exception is focus on an interactive control, and BODY is not one. The harness supplying the attribute is an environmental trigger, and the rubric says that does not make the observed behavior conforming. The record still states it &#39;was a harness error, not a product/environment failure. No product finding.&#39; That misstates the repository fact: the product&#39;s own exclusion logic produced the non-advance. The rubric directs a fail for this criterion when a reproduced violation is called not a finding. Judges A and B call the harness-error label correct, but line 903 shows the product behavior itself was observed. Their reasons, the careful labelling of attribution-URL inference and static inspection, do not decide this.","evidence":["Line 903: &#39;PageDown, target BODY, defaultPrevented=false, index stayed 6 with tabindex=-1; after removing the injected tabindex, PageDown advanced 6→7. Entities present in only one of two adjacent steps SHALL animate in or out.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Persisting entity morphs\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same identity exists in two consecutive steps\\n- **THEN** navigating between them animates that entity from its old state (position, size, label, emphasis) to its new state in place\\n\\n#### Scenario: New entity enters after others settle\\n- **WHEN** a step introduces a new entity\\n- **THEN** it animates in after the persisting entities have moved to their new positions\\n\\n#### Scenario: Departing entity exits\\n- **WHEN** an entity exists in a step but not in the next step\\n- **THEN** it animates out on that transition\\n\\n### Requirement: Persistent grouped scenes\\nAdjacent steps that represent successive states of the same evolving diagram SHALL be able to share a scene group so that the scene component persists while only the active step data changes. Shared groups prevent the whole scene from remounting between beats and preserve entity continuity for layout morphs.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Grouped steps update in place\\n- **WHEN** adjacent steps share a scene group and the same scene component\\n- **THEN** navigating between those steps updates the existing scene instance with the new step state rather than remounting separate scenes\\n\\n#### Scenario: Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same stable identity continues across grouped steps\\n- **THEN** it morphs through layout projection without being wrapped in newcomer fade-in behavior\\n\\n#### Scenario: Intentional composition is preserved\\n- **WHEN** a grouped scene intentionally overlaps or stacks entities\\n- **THEN** the implementation preserves that composition while maintaining clean morphs, rather than flattening or spreading entities only to satisfy an implementation pattern\\n\\n### Requirement: Style ownership boundary\\nThe scene kit SHALL have zero styling defaults. It SHALL provide motion behavior, fixed-canvas layout plumbing, navigation/chrome behavior, and stable DOM hooks for authors to style, but it SHALL NOT impose a palette, font, color, border treatment, glow, card appearance, button style, spacing scale, CSS theme tokens, or styling-framework dependency. Any default geometry used for the fixed canvas or chrome placement is layout behavior, not a visual style system.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Kit primitives expose style hooks\\n- **WHEN** a presentation composes scene kit primitives or chrome\\n- **THEN** the rendered markup exposes stable hooks that presentation-owned CSS can target\\n- **AND** visual choices such as color, typography, spacing scale, borders, and shadows come from the presentation or host app\\n\\n#### Scenario: Unstyled kit output\\n- **WHEN** a presentation uses scene kit primitives without presentation-owned CSS\\n- **THEN** the kit does not supply fallback colors, fonts, borders, shadows, card treatments, or button treatments\\n\\n#### Scenario: Optional styling frameworks remain optional\\n- **WHEN** a presentation author wants to use Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **THEN** that framework is configured by the presentation or host app, not required by the reusable scene kit\\n\\n#### Scenario: Coordinate-heavy diagrams are supported\\n- **WHEN** a presentation needs literal per-step coordinates for diagram entities\\n- **THEN** kit primitives expose class/style hooks, and authors MAY use raw motion elements with stable `layoutId`s when a primitive is not the right shape\\n\\n### Requirement: Kit attribution\\nThe scene kit SHALL include a default attribution link reading \\\"made by and-scene\\\" in the bottom-right corner, linking to the and-scene GitHub repository. The attribution is toolkit disclosure, not a presentation style system. The kit SHALL expose a stable hook so presentation-owned CSS can make the attribution legible and intentional. The kit SHALL NOT add a default top-left \\\"and-scene\\\" brand link; host applications MAY provide their own header brand explicitly.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default attribution is shown\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without overriding attribution options\\n- **THEN** it shows a bottom-right link labeled \\\"made by and-scene\\\" pointing to the and-scene GitHub repository\\n\\n#### Scenario: Attribution exposes a styling hook\\n- **WHEN** the default attribution is rendered\\n- **THEN** it exposes a stable presentation hook that the presentation or host app can target for local styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Top-left brand is opt-in\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without host-provided branding\\n- **THEN** the top-left header slot does not contain a default and-scene brand link\\n\\n### Requirement: Present and browse modes\\nA presentation SHALL support a present mode for live delivery and a browse mode for self-guided reading, switchable at runtime, and MAY declare which mode it opens in.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Present mode is title-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in present mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its marker and one-line title, with the caption, table of contents, and prev/next controls hidden\\n\\n#### Scenario: Browse mode is reading-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in browse mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its title, multi-line caption, a table of contents on wide viewports, prev/next controls, and step progress indicators\\n\\n#### Scenario: Mode toggle preserves position\\n- **WHEN** the user toggles the mode\\n- **THEN** the presentation switches between present and browse while staying on the current step\\n\\n### Requirement: Step navigation\\nA presentation SHALL let the viewer move between steps via keyboard, touch, and on-screen controls, and SHALL allow jumping directly to a step or section.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Keyboard navigation\\n- **WHEN** the user presses Right, Space, or PageDown\\n- **THEN** the presentation advances one step; and WHEN the user presses Left or PageUp THEN it goes back one step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Touch swipe\\n- **WHEN** the user swipes horizontally\\n- **THEN** swiping left advances and swiping right goes back\\n\\n#### Scenario: Direct jump\\n- **WHEN** the user activates a progress indicator or a table-of-contents entry\\n- **THEN** the presentation jumps directly to that step, or to the first step of that section's era for a table-of-contents entry\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active navigation state is exposed\\n- **WHEN** a progress indicator or table-of-contents entry represents the active step\\n- **THEN** it exposes semantic current-step state and a stable active-state hook for presentation-owned styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Controls keep their keys\\n- **WHEN** focus is on an interactive control\\n- **THEN** navigation keys drive that control rather than also advancing the deck\\n\\n### Requirement: Boundary behavior\\nNavigation SHALL clamp at both ends with no wrap-around.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at start\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the first step and the user goes back\\n- **THEN** it stays on the first step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at end\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the last step and the user advances\\n- **THEN** it stays on the last step\\n\\n### Requirement: Fixed-canvas fit scaling\\nThe diagram SHALL be composed in a fixed design canvas and scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow and entity morphs stay clean across viewport sizes. The default design canvas SHALL be 880 × 380, with per-mode fit geometry for the browse and present layouts.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Uniform scaling on resize\\n- **WHEN** the viewport size changes\\n- **THEN** the diagram scales uniformly to fit without reflowing its internal composition\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default canvas dimensions\\n- **WHEN** a presentation does not override the design canvas\\n- **THEN** it uses the default dimensions of 880 × 380\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":801,"end_line":814,"lines":[{"line":801,"text":"# Acceptance findings — round 0"},{"line":802,"text":""},{"line":803,"text":"Tested revision: `0f8a469109644a1b805424f8d91086e0a89e02fa`."},{"line":804,"text":""},{"line":805,"text":"## F-001 — Diagram labels become unreadable at a phone viewport"},{"line":806,"text":""},{"line":807,"text":"- **Severity:** Medium; visual usability defect."},{"line":808,"text":"- **Affected behavior:** Reference sample composition on narrow viewports (`presentation-skill`: visual composition check; generated quality bar)."},{"line":809,"text":"- **Expected:** The key scene remains visually coherent and its important content can be read during the required narrow-viewport review."},{"line":810,"text":"- **Observed:** At 390×844, the 880×380 canvas uniformly scales to fit a 342px stage width. The scene stays inside the viewport with no horizontal overflow, but entity labels and card text shrink to a few pixels and cannot be read. This is reproducible in both browse and present mode."},{"line":811,"text":"- **Reproduction:** Open `/how-to-make-a-presentation`, resize to 390×844, navigate to step 5, inspect the diagram labels; toggle to present mode and inspect again."},{"line":812,"text":"- **Evidence:** `acceptance-screenshots/mobile-step-05.png`, `acceptance-screenshots/mobile-present-step-05.png`."},{"line":813,"text":"- **Tested SHA:** `0f8a469109644a1b805424f8d91086e0a89e02fa`."},{"line":814,"text":""}],"label":"[artifact candidate-f1db9484c4d91a01 (findings-history)]"}]},"audit_results":[{"id":"assumption-repository-facts-distinguished","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"Line 903 records a run where PageDown was pressed with focus on BODY.
